transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-08-07 16:00 PDT
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood CSM), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood Onboarding), Priya Nair (Lakemore CTO), Ethan Brooks (Head of ML), Sofia Martinez (Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (Security)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Redwood and Lakemore align on initial pilot to run in staging, plan to peer VPC for private deployment, discuss SOC2 artifacts, and agree handoff to SE for technical deep dive.

00:00 - Speaker 1 (Avery Chen): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Avery, I'll be your CSM. With me are Ravi and Maya. How's everyone doing?
00:08 - Priya Nair: Doing good, thanks. Appreciate you squeezing us in, we wanted to get clarity on networking and what the pilot looks like.
00:14 - Ravi Patel: Great. Quick agenda — review timeline, connectivity options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security needs, and pilot success criteria. Then next steps. Short ok?
00:24 - Ethan Brooks: Yep that's perfect. Our constraints: production needs to be VPC-isolated, can't send PII to third-party hosted endpoints. Latency target about sub-150ms median for 500ms p95 for our search use-case. Cost is a factor but security > cost for now.
00:41 - Maya Lopez: Understood. Typical path we've seen is staging in our hosted but private VPC peering for the pilot so you can run data through a private lane, then move to dedicated or on-prem if required.
00:58 - Sofia Martinez: Quick clarifying q: when you say private VPC peering do you mean Redwood Private with our own control plane or just peering to Hosted? We need a diagram.
01:08 - Ravi Patel: Good question. There's two common patterns — 1) hosted with VPC peering (control plane managed by Redwood but data plane in your VPC via an egress endpoint) or 2) Redwood Private which is a customer-controlled control plane deployed in your cloud or on-prem. For pilot we often recommend the peering hosted path to move faster. We'll share a network diagram.
01:28 - Liam O'Connor: From security side if we do hosted peering we need KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, SAML SSO, RBAC controls. Also SOC2 artifacts, retention policy, and data residency confirmation.
01:44 - Avery Chen: Yep we can provide SOC2, ISO attestation, and the audit logs playbook. For KMS we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for Private and we can discuss partial KMS options on Hosted. Expect some nuance there.
01:58 - Priya Nair: Also timeline — we want the pilot running in staging within two weeks. Is that realistic?
02:05 - Maya Lopez: Yes two weeks is aggressive but doable if Lakemore can provide network CIDRs and approve some firewall rules quickly. We'll provision a staging tenant and do an SE deep dive within that window.
02:18 - Ethan Brooks: We'll definitely move on getting those details. Another thing — performance: can you run a quick benchmark with our prompt set? We might need quantization or a different model variant.
02:30 - Ravi Patel: Absolutely. Typical flow — we ingest your prompt set in a benchmark harness, run throughput and latency tests against a couple model profiles. For inference engine we have a few optimized kernels for attention and kv-cache performance — sorry that jargon is sometimes rough in the transcript — but we'll tune per workload.
02:49 - Priya Nair: Good. On the legal side procurement asked about data deletion guarantees and retention windows. Anyone from legal on call? Not today.
02:58 - Avery Chen: We can share the Data Processing Addendum and retention policy. We'll flag the legal contact for follow-up.
03:07 - 00:03:08 - Speaker 2 (Ethan): Is there any thought about dedicated capacity? We have bursts in end-of-quarter reports, occasionally spikes to 3x baseline.
03:16 - Ravi Patel: For bursts Dedicated with burst capacity or autoscaling pools is the best safety valve for consistent latency. For pilot we suggest hosted-peering but with routing policies set to fall back to a lower-cost model if capacity constrained.
03:30 - Sofia Martinez: Can we pin a model version? We need deterministic behavior for A/B tests.
03:36 - Maya Lopez: Yes model pinning and rollout controls are supported — can do canary rollouts and pin to a checksumed model artifact. We'll add that to the runbook.
03:44 - Priya Nair: Ok great. Quick clarifying: where do we upload our evaluation prompt sets and how do you handle eval regressions?
03:52 - Ravi Patel: You can upload to the evals dashboard in Console; we run nightly regression checks and can set threshold alerts. We'll show you the Console access in the SE deep dive.
04:03 - Liam O'Connor: About logging — can you stream token-level logs to our SIEM or do you only provide aggregate metrics?
04:11 - Avery Chen: We can provide both. Token-level tracing can be enabled in staging for debugging with retention controls; for prod we usually recommend sampled traces unless your compliance mandates full traces.
04:24 - Priya Nair: I'll need the SOC2 package and the network diagram. Also our security team needs to confirm if RedWood supports hardware HSM KMS — important for regulated data.
04:35 - Ravi Patel: We support BYOK with cloud KMSs and HSM integrations for Private deployments; for hosted peering we'll propose a KMS flow that meets encryption-in-transit and at-rest needs. We'll follow up with the HSM differentiator doc.
04:50 - Ethan Brooks: For the pilot success metric let's define: 1) Integration completed in staging, 2) Latency p50 < 150ms and p95 < 500ms on the defined prompt set, 3) No PII exfiltration detected in audit, 4) Basic A/B evaluation sample accuracy within 3% of baseline.
05:12 - Maya Lopez: Nice, we'll add that as the pilot success criteria.
05:18 - Priya Nair: Are there any blockers we should be aware of?
05:23 - Avery Chen: Biggest blocker typically network approvals and firewall whitelists; latency tuning might need model variant changes which we can iterate on.
05:31 - Sofia Martinez: We'll have firewall and CIDRs ready by Monday (2026-08-10).
05:36 - Raven? (laughter) — sorry mislabel, 05:39 - Ravi Patel: No worries.
05:40 - 00:05:41 - Discussion / small crosstalk about calendar invites
07:02 - Ravi Patel: Technical note — when peering, we use a private egress endpoint with mutual TLS to our runtime, and you can run inference traffic without public internet egress. We'll share sample terraform and a checklist.
07:18 - Liam O'Connor: That mutual TLS detail helps. For audit we need request IDs for traceability.
07:24 - Ravi Patel: We emit request IDs in headers and in the tracing logs; you can correlate with SSO user IDs if you pass identity through.
07:33 - Priya Nair: Ok. Any other compliance packages? We may need extra retention for some datasets for 7 years.
07:41 - Avery Chen: Retention policies are configurable in Private; hosted has standard retention tiers and an enterprise archiving addon — we'll include options.
07:53 - Ethan Brooks: Timeline recap please — what are the immediate next steps?
07:57 - Avery Chen: Recap: 1) Lakemore to share CIDR blocks + allowlist (Sofia). 2) Redwood to provision staging tenant + share network diagram and terraform sample (Ravi). 3) Redwood to send SOC2 packet and HSM/KMS note (Avery). 4) Schedule SE deep dive (Ravi + Sofia) for 2026-08-12.
08:16 - Priya Nair: Sounds good. Please tee up the runbook with the model pinning instructions and the eval upload steps.
08:24 - Maya Lopez: Will do.
08:27 - 00:08:28 - Customer churn joke then quick laugh
08:40 - Sofia Martinez: One more thing — are there cost-estimation templates for token pricing and dedicated pool sizing?
08:47 - Ravi Patel: Yes we have an Optimize toolkit and a sizing worksheet. We'll populate it with your expected QPS and sequences and share a cost profile.
08:57 - Priya Nair: Great.
09:03 - Avery Chen: Anything else from Lakemore side?
09:06 - Ethan Brooks: No. We're good. Thanks everyone.
09:10 - Avery Chen: Thanks team — we'll follow up with the docs and next steps.

Transcript notes:
- Some auto labels were messy (Speaker 1/2). Transcription had a few mis-heard proper nouns (e.g., "kv cache" rendered as "k-v cash" in a few places).
- Natural pauses and filler words present; small cross talk when scheduling.

Final recap (verbatim style):
- Pilot scope: Staging tenant with VPC peering; run benchmark on provided prompt set; evaluate latency & accuracy; security sign-off.
- Timeline: Provision staging and share runbook by 2026-08-11, SE deep dive 2026-08-12, SOC2 docs by 2026-08-10-14 window.
- Owners: Avery — SOC2 + compliance packet; Ravi — network terraform + benchmark harness and deep dive; Sofia — provide network info and join deep dive; Priya — confirm legal recipients.

- Network diagram & terraform sample (link: https://redwood.example.com/network-examples/vpc-peering)
